posts.caption: Quoting, in one sentence. What would you add to the list? 👇
Every shop has had this exact conversation. 🤝
Cheap work isn't cheap. It's just paid for twice. Seen it?
The part is cheap. Knowing which part isn't. Where do you land on this? 👇
Customer wants the diagnostic fee waived “since you're already here.” The knowledge IS the product. Do you hold the line or eat it? 👇
The other guy's quote and yours aren't the same job. Homeowners find that out on visit #2. 🔧
The “friend price” is full price plus the headache. Every shop learns this once. What finally made you stop giving it? 👇
What's the worst “the last guy did it” job you've walked into? Photos absolutely encouraged. We'll feature the best (worst) ones. 👇
Found behind the drywall this week: a garden hose doing a P-trap's job. Rate the previous install 1–10. I'll start — it's on fire. 🔥
Opened a panel today and found wire nuts holding things together like a craft project. What's the scariest thing you've found behind a wall? 👇
Flex tape on a supply line isn't a repair — it's a countdown. Post the worst “temporary fix” you've inherited. 👇
Homeowner “saved money” doing it himself. Now I'm charging double to undo it. What's the most expensive DIY you've had to rip back out? 👇
Drop your best before/after. Any trade — roof, panel, re-pipe, install, cleanout. Let's see the work that doesn't get enough credit. 👇
Nobody claps when it's done right — the light just turns on, the water just drains. Post the job you were proudest of that no one noticed. 👇
Drop the runner-up below. 👇
Plumbers, you're up first. The rest of us are not ready. 👇
There is no “just quickly.” Every trade knows it. What's the line that makes you brace? 👇
It looked easy in the video. That's the whole business model. 😅
The magic words: “my neighbor's guy.” Cool. Go call him. 👇
“Can we do cash and skip the paperwork?” The paperwork is what protects THEM. How do you explain that without losing the job? 👇
It's somewhere in the truck. It's always somewhere in the truck.
Every jobsite has “that guy.” What's his signature move? 👇
The “quick 30-minute job” has never once taken 30 minutes. Not once. What's your longest “quick” job? 👇
“Just one more thing before you go.” We all felt that in our spine. 😮‍💨
Put on a clean shirt for ONE estimate and somehow ended up crawling through 40 years of attic insulation. Every time. What's your version? 👇
Friday, 3pm, phone rings — emergency call. You taking it or letting it ring? No wrong answers. 👇
Settle it in the comments. We're not picking sides. (Yes we are.) 👇
Work-truck edition. Choose your fighter. This will not stay civil. 👇
You lend tools on a jobsite: never / to a chosen few / to anyone with a pulse? The wrong answer is how you lose a $200 impact. 👇
One tool you'd run back into a burning truck for. Go. 👇
Every crew has the guy who guards the radio like it's a hostage situation. What's the ONE song that starts a jobsite fight? 👇
We all know him. Tag him (gently). 👇

Posted for a helper. Three no-shows and one guy who quit because I asked him to sweep. The trades don't have a wage problem — they have a “show up” problem. Who's actually hiring right now? Drop your city. 👇
Guy accepted the job, said “see you Monday,” vanished. It's not a labor shortage, it's a follow-through shortage. Who's reliable and actually looking? Drop your city. 👇
Hardest part of running a shop this year: finding work / finding good help / getting paid on time? Pick your poison. 👇
Slow-season survival rule #1: the time to market is when you're busy, not when the phone stops. The work you book in summer fills January. What are you doing NOW to stay booked through winter? 👇

Three ways shops bleed money they never see:

1. Unbilled change orders
2. “Quick favors” that aren't quick
3. Not charging for the drive

Which one's getting you this year? 👇
Third month chasing a customer for a $4k invoice. At what point is it worth the lien? Asking for me, honestly. 👇
No deposit, no material order. I learned that with $6k of custom material sitting in my garage. What's your deposit rule? 👇
The best time to ask for the Google review is the second the customer says “wow, looks great” — not three days later by text. When do YOU ask? 👇
